reasons: Deviation classification is correct: § 12.4 is one-sided (binds only Customer), runs 18 months from termination, covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel involved in the Services, bars 'engaging' (a no-hire) and lacks any general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — it fails the fallback on every material term and the no-hire/all-personnel scope is walk-away territory.

Redline lands squarely on the fallback: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, twelve months from the end of involvement, no-hire deleted, and general-advertising plus unsolicited-approach carve-outs added.
The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (ratio 0.819) is expected here — the original clause could not reach the fallback without a full rewrite, and no unrelated terms were altered.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice; the noted conflict with § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer made no no-hire commitment) is a genuine internal inconsistency supporting the edit.
No double-flagging or benefit-to-our-party issue; the mutualised restriction is the playbook-sanctioned fallback rather than a self-inflicted burden.
